description: Search live Commonplace inventory by words, category, place (deliver_to alone returns some listings near it, not every one), or any mix. Results are active and buyable. outcome: ok; none; none_within_limits (every match is in hidden); out_of_budget (matches only outside the price range; examples ignore deliver_to); undeliverable (none reaches deliver_to; examples say how far). With deliver_to, each result carries delivery (known, deliverable, driving distance_miles, fee_usd, total_usd). Candidates come from the words or categories plus the catalogue's proximity ranking, not the whole catalogue: to be thorough, also search category_hint and its department. Up to 40 are checked per call, roughly nearest first; with max_distance_miles, one already well past it in a straight line is not checked but counted in too_far (distance_is_straight_line: a lower bound, not a drive). delivery_checked, candidates_considered and candidates_unchecked (could be inside the limits, never checked) say how far it got; next_offset, passed back as offset, checks the rest. cheapest and most_expensive spend all 40 checks and return the best (results_not_shown counts the rest; a limit up to 40 returns them); any sort orders only what was checked. farthest_checked_miles, the longest drive measured, can pass the radius. `hidden` counts every candidate left out, once each, by reason, with its nearest or cheapest examples. When no title matches, the category the words point to is browsed (no_title_matched) or the outcome is none; matched_on names looser words that matched. more_available: candidates_unchecked (see next_offset), or more_matches_unread: more listings match than one search reads, which offset cannot reach; narrow the words, category or price.

category.description: Only these categories: a slug from catalog_list_categories, listing_resolve_category or a result's category_slug, or several separated by commas (sofas,sectionals,general-furniture). A department (furniture) or parent (peloton) covers every category beneath it, and a category covers the older slugs its listings are stored under (peloton-bike returns peloton-bike-2nd-gen listings). With words too, only this category is searched, and words matching nothing in it return none.

deliver_to.description: Where it would be delivered: a 5-digit ZIP or "City, ST". Keeps only items that can be delivered there, which can be far away. To find items near a place, give the place here with max_distance_miles.

hidden_examples.description: How many listings each hidden reason shows (default 10 for too_far, 20 for the others); counts are always complete.

limit.description: How many listings to return (default 5, at most 40).

max_distance_miles.description: With deliver_to: only items within this many driving miles of it.

max_price_usd.description: Highest price, inclusive, in US dollars: buyer_price_usd, or with deliver_to the total with delivery. A listing whose buyer price alone is over it is not a candidate at all. For "under $1,200", pass 1199.99.

min_price_usd.description: Lowest buyer_price_usd, inclusive, in US dollars. Always compared with buyer_price_usd, with or without deliver_to.

offset.description: With deliver_to: a previous call's next_offset, with the same other arguments, to check the candidates it did not reach (hidden then counts only that call's checks). Use it rather than price bands to be thorough: min_price_usd compares the price before delivery, so bands can miss a listing.

query.description: What to look for, e.g. "peloton bike+" or "sectional sofa". Words match titles loosely, with only a few everyday synonyms (couch and sofa, fridge and refrigerator) ("hot tub" misses a listing titled Jacuzzi: search its category), though "+" and "plus" count as the same. Optional when category is given: without words, the search browses the category.

sort.description: best_match is relevance order and says nothing about price. With deliver_to, cheapest orders by the delivered total and nearest by driving distance (nearest needs deliver_to).
